sections.title: Weighing Choices: Mit tegyek? Hová forduljunk?
sections.content: When a speaker faces a moral dilemma or asks for counsel about what course of action to take ('What should I do?', 'Whom shall we turn to?'), Hungarian uses the 1st person singular (-jak/-jek) or 1st person plural (-junk/-jünk) subjunctive-imperative mood. Unlike kellene + infinitive, which sounds analytical, the deliberative subjunctive conveys immediate personal agency and dramatic urgency.

sections.title: Indignant Echo Questions in Confrontation
sections.content: In heated dialogue, the subjunctive is also used in echo questions to reject an unreasonable demand or accusation with disbelief: Én kérjek bocsánatot, amikor ő sértett meg engem? ('Am I supposed to apologize when he insulted me?'), Tétlenül nézzük, ahogy tönkreteszik a művészetet? ('Are we to watch idly as they ruin art?').

sections.title: Deliberative vs. Indignant Subjunctive Questions
rows: Mit tegyek ebben a kilátástalan helyzetben?
What am I to do in this hopeless situation?
Kihez forduljunk, ha a bíróság is hallgat?
Whom should we turn to if even the court remains silent?
Én mondjak le az elveimről a siker kedvéért?
Am I supposed to give up my principles for the sake of success?
Hogyan győzzem meg őket, ha nem hallgatnak az észérvekre?
How am I to convince them if they don't listen to rational arguments?

items.spanish: Hallgassak tovább, vagy tárjam fel végre a kellemetlen igazságot?
items.english: Should I keep silent any longer, or finally reveal the unpleasant truth?

items.spanish: Milyen érvekkel cáfoljuk meg ezt az alaptalan vádat?
items.english: With what arguments shall we refute this baseless accusation?

items.spanish: Mi viseljük a felelősséget mások mulasztásáért?
items.english: Are we supposed to bear the responsibility for others' negligence?

items.spanish: Kinek higgyek, ha mindenki másképp meséli el a történteket?
items.english: Whom should I believe if everyone tells the story differently?

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Notice the contrast between 'Mit csinálok?' ('What am I doing?' — indicative present) and 'Mit csináljak?' ('What should I do?' — deliberative subjunctive).
